about: Lesson bank for the daily reel. Each verse is in the IIT Kanpur numbering and passes reels/tools/verse.py verify. 'used' marks lessons already made; the daily run takes the first unused one, or adds a new verified entry when the bank runs low.

verse.sanskrit:
न वनं गन्तुकामस्य त्यजतश्च वसुन्धराम् ।
सर्वलोकातिगस्येव लक्ष्यते चित्तविक्रिया ॥
verse.translation: Setting out for the forest, giving up the whole earth, he showed no sign of inner turmoil, like one who has risen above all the worlds.

lessons.context: Exiled on the eve of his coronation, Rama's face doesn't change (19.32 moon simile, 19.36).
lessons.lesson: Keep your peace when you lose.

verse.sanskrit:
कथञ्चिदुपकारेण कृतेनैकेन तुष्यति ।
न स्मरत्यपकाराणां शतमप्यात्मवत्तया ॥
verse.translation: He is pleased by a single kindness, however it was done, and, being self-possessed, he does not remember even a hundred wrongs.

lessons.context: Valmiki's portrait of Rama in the opening of the Ayodhya Kanda.

verse.sanskrit:
कच्चिदर्थं विनिश्चित्य लघुमूलं महोदयम् ।
क्षिप्रमारभसे कर्तुं न दीर्घयसि राघव ॥
verse.translation: Having settled on a goal that costs little and yields much, do you start on it quickly and not drag it out, Raghava?

lessons.context: Rama questions Bharata at Chitrakuta (sarga 100 is a whole checklist: 100.18 sleep, 100.19 counsel).

verse.sanskrit:
गच्छानुजानामि रणार्दितस्त्वं प्रविश्य रात्रिंचरराज लङ्काम् ।
आश्वास्य निर्याहि रथी च धन्वी तदा बलं द्रक्ष्यसि मे रथस्थः ॥
verse.translation: Go, I let you go, worn out by battle as you are. Enter Lanka, king of the night-rangers, catch your breath, then come out again with chariot and bow; then, from your chariot, you will see my strength.

lessons.context: First duel: Rama cuts Ravana's bow and crown, then lets him go (59.139-144).

verse.sanskrit:
तद्ब्रूहि वचनं देवि राज्ञो यदभिकाङ्क्षितम् ।
करिष्ये प्रतिजाने च रामो द्विर्नाभिभाषते ॥
verse.translation: Tell me, queen, what the king wants. I will do it, I promise. Rama does not say things twice.

lessons.context: Before he even hears the demand, Rama tells Kaikeyi he will do it.

verse.sanskrit:
स च नित्यं प्रशान्तात्मा मृदुपूर्वं तु भाषते ।
उच्यमानोऽपि परुषं नोत्तरं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
verse.translation: Always calm, he speaks gently first; even when spoken to harshly, he does not answer back.

lessons.context: Valmiki's portrait of Rama.

verse.sanskrit:
स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषी च धर्मं सर्वात्मना श्रितः ।
सम्यग्योक्ता श्रेयसां च न विगृह्य कथारुचिः ॥
verse.translation: He speaks first, with a smile; he holds to dharma with his whole being; he pursues what is good in the right way, and has no taste for quarrelsome talk.

lessons.context: Dasharatha's council describes the prince.
lessons.lesson: Start conversations kindly; skip the arguments.

verse.sanskrit:
उत्सवेषु च सर्वेषु पितेव परितुष्यति ।
सत्यवादी महेष्वासो वृद्धसेवी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
verse.translation: At every festival he rejoices like a father. He speaks the truth, is a great archer, serves his elders, and masters his senses.

lessons.context: The people's view of Rama (2.40 says he grieves deeply at others' misfortunes).

verse.sanskrit:
मरणान्तानि वैराणि निर्वृत्तं नः प्रयोजनम् ।
क्रियतामस्य संस्कारो ममाप्येष यथा तव ॥
verse.translation: Enmity ends with death. Our purpose is done. Let his last rites be performed; he is as much mine as yours.

lessons.context: Rama tells Vibhishana to give Ravana full funeral honours.
lessons.lesson: Let it end when it ends.

verse.sanskrit:
सत्यमेवेश्वरो लोके सत्यं पद्मा श्रिता सदा ।
सत्यमूलानि सर्वाणि सत्यान्नास्ति परं पदम् ॥
verse.translation: Truth alone is the lord in this world; prosperity always rests on truth. Truth is the root of everything; there is nothing higher than truth.

lessons.context: Rama answers Jabali, who urged him to break his word and go home.

verse.sanskrit:
सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः ।
संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं च जीवितम् ॥
verse.translation: Every hoard ends in loss, every rise ends in a fall, every meeting ends in parting, and life ends in death.

lessons.context: Rama consoles grieving Bharata after Dasharatha's death.
lessons.lesson: Nothing lasts, so hold things lightly.

verse.sanskrit:
यथा काष्ठं च काष्ठं च समेयातां महार्णवे ।
समेत्य च व्यपेयातां कालमासाद्य कञ्चन ॥
verse.translation: As one log meets another on the great ocean, and after some time they drift apart again...

lessons.context: Rama to Bharata: family, friends and wealth meet us and part from us like this (105.27).
lessons.lesson: People drift; love them while they are here.

verse.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्निद्रावशं नैषि कच्चित्काले प्रबुध्यसे ।
कच्चिच्चापररात्रेषु चिन्तयस्यर्थनैपुणम् ॥
verse.translation: I hope you are not ruled by sleep, and wake at the right time? And in the last hours of the night, do you think about how to do things well?

lessons.context: Chitrakuta checklist.

verse.sanskrit:
कच्चिन्मन्त्रयसे नैकः कच्चिन्न बहुभिः सह ।
कच्चित्ते मन्त्रितो मन्त्रो राष्ट्रं न परिधावति ॥
verse.translation: Do you take counsel neither alone nor with too many? And does your plan not run all over the kingdom before it is carried out?

lessons.context: Chitrakuta checklist.

verse.sanskrit:
उपकारफलं मित्रम् अपकारोऽरिलक्षणम् ।
अद्यैव तं वधिष्यामि तव भार्यापहारिणम् ॥
verse.translation: Help is the fruit of friendship; harm is the mark of an enemy. This very day I will slay the one who took your wife.

lessons.context: Rama's pact with Sugriva.

verse.sanskrit:
रामो विग्रहवान् धर्मः साधुः सत्यपराक्रमः ।
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य देवानामिव वासवः ॥
verse.translation: Rama is dharma in bodily form, good, truly valiant, the king of the whole world as Indra is of the gods.

lessons.context: Maricha, on Ravana's side, warns Ravana about Rama.
lessons.lesson: Be someone even your rivals respect.

verse.sanskrit:
स च सर्वगुणोपेतः कौसल्यानन्दवर्धनः ।
समुद्र इव गाम्भीर्ये धैर्येण हिमवानिव ॥
verse.translation: Endowed with every virtue, he deepens Kausalya's joy; deep as the ocean, steady as the Himalaya.

lessons.context: Narada describes Rama to Valmiki.

verse.sanskrit:
कोन्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् ।
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः ॥
verse.translation: Who in this world today is virtuous and also valiant, knows dharma, is grateful, truthful and firm in his vows?

lessons.context: Valmiki's question to Narada that starts the whole epic.

verse.sanskrit:
पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणां प्लवङ्गम ।
कार्यं करुणमार्येण न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति ॥
verse.translation: Whether they are wicked or good, or even deserve to die, O monkey, a noble person should act with compassion; there is no one who never does wrong.

lessons.context: Sita stops Hanuman from punishing the rakshasis who guarded her.
lessons.lesson: Mercy is strength (a lesson from Sita).

verse.sanskrit:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलमनिर्वेदः परं सुखम् ।
अनिर्वेदो हि सततं सर्वार्थेषु प्रवर्तकः ॥
verse.translation: Not losing heart is the root of success; not losing heart is the highest happiness. Not losing heart is what always drives us in every task.

lessons.context: Hanuman, failing to find Sita in Lanka, refuses to give up.
lessons.lesson: Don't quit (a lesson from Hanuman's search for Rama's wife).

verse.sanskrit:
न दोषं त्वयि पश्यामि सूक्ष्ममप्यरिसूदन ।
न चापि जननीं बाल्यात्त्वं विगर्हितुमर्हसि ॥
verse.translation: I don't see the slightest fault in you, slayer of foes. Nor should you, out of childishness, blame your mother.

lessons.context: Rama defends Kaikeyi to Bharata.
lessons.lesson: Defend people even when they hurt you.

verse.sanskrit:
मुनीनामन्यथा कर्तुं सत्यमिष्टं हि मे सदा ।
अप्यहं जीवितं जह्यां त्वां वा सीते सलक्ष्मणाम् ॥
verse.translation: ...to go back on my word to the sages: truth is always dear to me. I could give up my life, or you, Sita, with Lakshmana (but never a promise, 10.19).

lessons.context: Sita questions Rama's vow to protect the forest sages.
